applied.fact: Wilderness self-issue permit and Discover Pass

access.fees: No trailhead fee; the private timberland road beyond the gate requires the landowner's fee recreation access permit
access.rules: Once inside the Mount Baker Wilderness boundary, no mechanized travel (including bikes) is permitted — bike use on the approach is only legal on the non-Wilderness logging-road miles
access.permit: Free self-issue Wilderness permit at the trailhead register (route lies within Mount Baker Wilderness)
access.closures: FR 38 (Middle Fork Road) has had seasonal gate closures (roughly Nov 1-Jul 1) on portions to protect wildlife in past years, and was significantly damaged by washouts in the December 2025 floods; it has been closed to vehicles at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026 — check current status with the Mt. Baker Ranger District before driving
access.landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mt. Baker Ranger District
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
access.parking_pass: No developed fee trailhead here — FR 38 gate/pullout is an undeveloped roadside parking spot; no Northwest Forest Pass required.
access.passRequired: No Northwest Forest Pass required at the FR 38 quarry-road pullouts (not a developed recreation site)

overnight_permit.where: Camping is on unregulated Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest land (camping is not allowed on the private timberland below it); no wilderness permit or registration is needed. The Dailey Prairie logging-road gate is separately locked to vehicles by the timber company, which is an access issue unrelated to camping.

access.fees: Fee recreational access permit required for the Hampton timberland approach (myoutdooragent.com, ~79,000 acres across Whatcom/Skagit/Snohomish counties)
access.rules: Pack out human waste (blue bags) — no burial or glacier deposition.
access.permit: Wilderness self-issue permit typically required within the Mount Baker Wilderness boundary
access.closures: Access road has historically been gated with 'No Trespassing / Permit Required' signage by the timberland owner; confirm current gate and permit status before approaching
access.landManager: Private industrial timberland (Hampton Family Forests / Hampton Lumber, on former Weyerhaeuser Columbia Timberlands) for the lower approach roads; Mount Baker Wilderness (Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, USFS) for the upper mountain
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
access.passRequired: Hampton recreational access permit; Northwest Forest Pass/America the Beautiful pass may apply at USFS trailhead facilities
